messages:
maria: Quick check — I'm planning to flip the burst + queueing flags for a limited canary at 11:00 PT. Proposed config: burst_enabled=true (2% traffic), queueing_weight=0.2, max_concurrency_guardrail=250. Canaries limited to dedicated accounts only. Any objections or red flags?

aj: Quick Qs — is the canary audience just the dedicated pool or also internal dev accounts? Where's the flag config stored (repo/dir)? Also can we have telemetry on queue_wait_ms and per-model concurrency?

maria: Canaries = dedicated pool only. Flag is in infra/feature-flags/rollouts.yaml (PR ready). Telemetry plan: queue_wait_ms, queue_depth, per-model tail P95 latency, error_rate.

kevin: Oncall FYI — I'll watch queue_depth and slot_wait_ms. If queue_depth > 100 for 5m -> page. Also recommend temporary suppressions for noisy models during the canary. Can someone add a per-model override for long-seq models?

sasha: ML note — for the 7B+s with long sequences, burst + queueing at these params can push them over CPU memory threshold. I'll add a per-model max_concurrency override (80) in model-profiles before the flip.

aj: I'll attach the short playbook steps to the PR. Rollout steps I have in mind:
- enable flag in infra for canary (2%)
- enable queueing_weight=0.2
- monitor key metrics for 15m
- escalate/rollback if queue_depth or tail latency regresses >30%

maria: What's the rollback flow? If we need to revert quickly, I want the exact commands.

aj: Rollback is simple: flip the flag off, and set queueing_weight back to 0 in the same commit. Command for deploy-bot:

```
/deploy toggle-flag --name burst_enabled --value false --scope canary --reason "rollback"
/deploy update-config --path infra/feature-flags/rollouts.yaml --set queueing_weight=0
```

That will disable new burst tokens and clear queueing. Existing inflight requests will drain.

kevin: Add one more safety: set a temporary guardrail that reduces canary to 0% automatically if any alert fires (queue_depth or p95_network). I can add a watcher script.

maria: Please do. Can you also add a short note in the runbook? link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/burst-rollouts (draft)

deploy-bot: deploy command queued by aj; awaiting approval.

maria: @kevin @sasha @aj I pushed PR #2387 with the flags + model overrides. Can you give quick thumbs or minor comments? Hoping to merge in 20m. :thumbsup:

kevin: Reviewing now, will ping if anything urgent.

sasha: LGTM on overrides, left one comment about the sequence-length threshold.

aj: Approved, added playbook snippet and monitoring dashboard link.

maria: Thanks — merging in 10. I'll post a short status update in #incidents if anything noisy shows up.

kevin: I'll keep oncall on standby for the first 30m.

maria: Rolling in 5. If anyone wants to observe metrics live, join the observability dashboard: https://observability.redwood/internal/dashboards/burst-canary

aj: Good luck :crossed_fingers: — ping here if you need a rollback.

maria: Done, merged and staging flip queued. deploy-bot, please run the canary enable steps at 11:00 PT.

deploy-bot: canary enable run scheduled for 11:00 PT. Logs will be posted here.

kevin: Saw a small bump in p95 for one model at +12% — watching.

sasha: I pushed a tweak to model override to drop that model's concurrency to 60.

maria: Noted. If it stabilizes in 10m we keep rolling, otherwise rollback.

kevin: 15m in — metrics look stable except that one model. No alerts.

maria: Keeping the canary running to 40m then widen to 10% if all good. Thanks all :rocket:
